title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 105-112). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic framework of 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier A carries a relation | (disjointness), a datum Delta, and an associated 'magasin' (store) F, a subset of P(A) whose members are 'figures'. Each element X of A has an associated element X^0 in a 'spatios' Sigma_A. Sigma_A is a lattice with sup, inf, 0, 1 and a complement ∁; the previous page uses passage to complements as if ∁ were an order-reversing involution.

On p.110 he defines a family (e_i)_{i in I} of mutually disjoint elements to be 'admissible' under the following condition. Put e = sup e_i, e_0 = ∁e, and e_{I'} = sup_{i in I'} e_i. Then for every splitting I = I' ⊔ I'' one must have ∁e_{I'} = e_{I''} ∨ e_0, equivalently e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''}. Under this condition the subalgebra generated is a Boolean algebra isomorphic to P(I ⊔ {0}).

This page states the first 'axiom of rapports' (the heading is most likely 'Axiome rapp. 1' rather than 'Atomisation 1'), labelled in the margin Figat(A). For every figure F in the store, the family (X^0)_{X in F} in Sigma_A is admissible. In other words, the 'shadows' in the spatios of the pieces of any figure behave like the atoms of a finite Boolean algebra. They do so together with the complement of their union.

He then claims the axiom is not redundant, via an example:
- Take a spatios Sigma.
- Take as atelier Figelspat_fin(Sigma), the finite (discrete) elementary spatial figures.
- Take as store Figspat_fin(Sigma), the finite spatial figures.
- By Cor. 1, the rapports axiom for this atelier amounts to a condition on pairs: if e | e' then e' = (∁e) ∧ (e ∨ e').

If ∁ is an orthocomplementation this is exactly the orthomodular law (take a = e', b = ∁e: a ≤ b implies a = b ∧ (∁b ∨ a)). The page breaks off with an incomplete sentence. It says that, by contrast, the validity of the conditions of Lemma 2 (p.105) on Sigma ... — presumably 'is not automatic', or 'is a stronger requirement'. Lemma 2 is the n-ary admissibility condition.

The next page strengthens the axiom using the refinement relation ≪ on finite discrete spatial figures. In short, the page serves the purpose of making 'figures' in an atelier behave like finite partitions, a combinatorial-lattice foundation for a geometry of figures.
errors: The non-redundancy argument is incomplete on the page: the sentence 'Par contre, la validité des conditions du lemme 2 (p.105) sur Σ.' has no main verb, so the counter-example is not actually produced.

Caveat: if ∁ in a spatios were a genuine orthocomplementation, the two-element (orthomodular) condition would already imply n-ary admissibility for all finite orthogonal families. This follows from the Foulis–Holland theorem: mutually orthogonal elements commute and generate a Boolean subalgebra. Non-redundancy can then only hold if ∁ is weaker, e.g. a closure-of-complement type operation with e ∧ ∁e ≠ 0. The page does not make explicit which situation obtains; this is unsure from this page alone.

ideas.what: Admissible families: mutually disjoint elements of a lattice with complement whose finite joins satisfy e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''}, so they generate a Boolean algebra isomorphic to P(I ⊔ {0})
ideas.modern_name: orthogonal family generating a Boolean subalgebra / finite partition of unity in an ortholattice
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936) for lattice logic; Foulis, Holland (1960s) for commuting families

ideas.what: Axiom: for each figure, the images X^0 of its constituents form an admissible family in the spatios
ideas.modern_name: partition/atomization axiom for an abstract figure calculus

ideas.what: Pairwise reduction of the axiom: e|e' ⇒ e' = ∁e ∧ (e ∨ e')

missed.claim: The condition to which the rapports axiom reduces for finite discrete spatial figures is, formally, the orthomodular law of quantum logic. The gap between this pairwise condition and the n-ary admissibility of Lemma 2 is exactly the territory of Foulis–Holland-type theorems. Grothendieck does not name this; his spatios framework is thus implicitly an orthomodular / De Morgan lattice setting.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anyone reconstructing the 'ateliers'/'spatios' program (a tame-topology foundation) could import orthomodular-lattice results. This would decide when the axioms are redundant, which matters precisely when ∁ is not an orthocomplement.

missed.claim: The non-redundancy counterexample (a spatios where the pairwise condition holds but Lemma 2 fails) is announced but not given; the sentence is cut off.
missed.quote: Par contre, la validité des conditions du lemme 2 (p. 105) sur Σ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small concrete lattice-theoretic question: exhibiting a De Morgan/closure-complement lattice that is 'orthomodular for pairs' but not admissible for triples. It is minor, but open within this framework.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a foundational axiom in Grothendieck's little-known 1986 'ateliers' theory; the theory as a whole is undocumented in the literature. The lattice content itself is elementary, and its reduction is the classical orthomodular law. The interest is mainly in the unrecognized link to quantum-logic lattices.
transcription_corrections: The underlined heading is more plausibly 'Axiome rapp. 1' (first axiom of rapports, matching 'le premier axiome sur les rapports') than 'Atomisation 1'.
'site[?] spatial Σ' should most likely read 'spatios Σ' (the next page uses 'un spatios Σ').
The final sentence 'Par contre, la validité des conditions du lemme 2 (p. 105) sur Σ.' is genuinely incomplete in the manuscript (no verb); it is not a transcription loss.
Marginal label is 'Figat(A)' (boxed), apparently naming the axiom or the structure (atelier with its figures).
